referenceSources.description:
A striking red and black Honda NSX GT500, car number 100, blasts down the circuit with sponsor decals from BP, Kenwood, and Advan. The aerodynamic bodywork, including a large rear wing and side vents, reflects the early JGTC modifications that transformed the road-going NSX into a competitive race machine. Team Kunimitsu’s entry was one of the few to run the 3.0L C30A V6 engine in 1996, marking Honda’s initial foray into GT500 competition.

This image is part of a comprehensive database chronicling NSX-GT evolution from 1996 to 2009. Over thirteen seasons, Honda experimented with naturally aspirated and twin-turbo engines, updated chassis designs, and navigated regulatory changes. The NSX-GT achieved multiple race wins, drivers’ and teams’ championships, and remained a JGTC/Super GT stalwart until its final appearance at Motegi in 2009.
